correctness.rationale: A reflected Brownian motion with generator f″, killed at 1, has occupation density 1−x when launched at 0. The time change with clock ∫(1/D) ds gives the specified natural-scale diffusion and the frozen objective, including bounded Borel D up to a.e. equality. For t=1−x and μ=1/c², strict convexity of t/d+μd outside the null set t=0 gives the unique box minimizer clip(c√t,ℓ,u). Integrating in t with splits at ℓ²/c² and, if active, u²/c² gives means 2c/3+ℓ³/(3c²) and u−(u³−ℓ³)/(3c²); both are strictly increasing in their active ranges and cover (ℓ,u). The upper layer has zero length at c=u. The same integrals for t/d give 2/(3c)−ℓ³/(6c⁴) and 1/(2u)+(u³−ℓ³)/(6c⁴). The two branches match along with F′=−1/c² and F″=3/(min(c,u)³−ℓ³); differentiating F″ gives the one-sided nonzero jump and shows F‴ does not exist at the threshold. Rescaling the generator on [0,L] supplies precisely the stated factor L² in physical passage time.
residual_risks: Requires the specified drift-free Itô generator, reflection and launch at 0, and strictly positive finite floor and ceiling; the proof does not compare whole passage-time distributions.

value.rationale: The clipped shape alone would be a standard multiplier calculation. The complete value law answers a practical design question the unbounded result cannot: when the ceiling binds in the presence of a positive floor, and what time penalty begins to accrue. For example, the proved jump says that relative to the floor-only optimum the cap penalty turns on cubically, with leading coefficient 9u⁵/[4(u³−ℓ³)³]. The threshold and marginal-budget behavior therefore supply concrete information beyond a restatement of the clipping rule.
residual_risks: This is an exact one-dimensional design calculation, not a general optimization method or a thermodynamic phase transition.
